scope: All-angular principal comparison operator and decisive obstruction to a fixed angular cutoff in the uncut relative form norm; not the full physical correction.
ordinary_argument_review: Start from the retained rank-two scalar spectral multiplier with the original common fourth finite part. It is not the full physical Hessian.
Partial fractions give the complete angular digamma sum; both roots have nonnegative real part and their coalescence is removable. Use the stable small-root expression.
Integrate the exact z derivative and exchange the alpha/v integrals to obtain a single positive-weight integral. Its weight mass fixes the coefficient against the existing a2 contact.
The exact counting function satisfies N(A)<=4A. Stieltjes integration bounds both first and second logarithmic derivatives by four, uniformly over all positive radial frequencies.
Log-linear interpolation with exact two weight moments gives the explicit uniform quadrature error. The first interval is controlled by the logarithmic derivative bound, not dropped or sampled.

Every finite angular cutoff has bounded K_N/p^4 while the full K/p^4 grows logarithmically. Thus the relative omitted principal-form norm is one and a truncated fourth-order inverse does not preserve operator order.

This obstruction concerns uncut continuum norms. It proves neither nonexistence nor physical high-frequency instability, and does not rule out direct residual certification of particular trial functions.
The exact fourth-power angular tail identity checks low-frequency normalization but supplies no uniform bound on the entire action-form unit ball.

Scalar bolt point sources and reflected mass/log boundary regularity remain. Spectral calculus for a closed Laplacian defines only the comparison operator; the complete physical boundary realization is not inferred from it.
The numerical thresholds certify principal-model approximation claims only. The full primal-dual correction, curved remainder and X/admission test remain unexecuted.
